$schema.description: Set it to https://glimmervoid.dev/schema/pack.v1.json so an editor completes and checks the file; Glimmervoid ignores it

name.description: Unique among installed packs; a second pack with the same name is refused. Theme and panel ids are scoped to it, so they never clash with another pack

version.description: Your release number, shown to the operator beside the pack; raise it with each change. Approval follows the files, not this number: any changed file asks again

description.description: One or two sentences shown on the pack card in the Packs tab and in the packs guide

preview.description: An image of what the pack adds, shown on its card in the Packs tab before it is approved. Glimmervoid releases after 0.58.4 read it; older ones refuse a manifest that sets it

requires.description: What this machine needs for the pack; while anything is missing the pack stays off here and its card says what, without counting as a problem in the pack

env.description: Environment variables the Glimmervoid server must have set

programs.description: Programs that must be on the PATH of the Glimmervoid server, such as gh or node

prFlows.description: PR flows this pack adds; one invalid entry skips the whole section

repos.description: The default owner/name repositories, matched case-insensitively, for every prAction, source and rule of this pack that lists no repos of its own; an entry's own repos narrow this default to the repositories both list; every repository when absent

prActions.description: Buttons on a pull request; the command prints {"outcome":"done|started|refused|failed","message":"..."}, and one that prints started reports later with glimmervoid pr-action report

id.description: Unique within its list; inside a pack it is shown as <pack>/<id>

label.description: The name shown to the operator; rules never match on it

command.description: The program and its arguments, run without a shell from the Glimmervoid home folder; an argument may hold {prUrl}, {repo}, {number}, {head}, {headRef}, {baseRef}, and in a pack also {packDir}, the pack's folder. Its environment has GLIMMERVOID_PR_URL, GLIMMERVOID_PR_REPO, GLIMMERVOID_PR_NUMBER and GLIMMERVOID_PR_HEAD, GLIMMERVOID_PR_HEAD_REF, GLIMMERVOID_PR_BASE_REF and the pull request as GLIMMERVOID_PR_JSON. Exit 0 means done and any other exit failed, unless stdout prints the action outcome JSON (glimmervoid packs guide --schema pr-flows)

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds before the command is stopped

repos.description: The owner/name repositories this applies to; every repository when absent

sources.description: Commands run on each pull request that print {"findings":[{"path","lineStart","lineEnd","priority","body","url"}],"status":[{"label","state"}]}, at most 200 findings and 4 status lines

id.description: Unique within its list; inside a pack it is shown as <pack>/<id>

label.description: The name shown to the operator; rules never match on it

command.description: The program and its arguments, run without a shell from the Glimmervoid home folder; an argument may hold {prUrl}, {repo}, {number}, {head}, and in a pack also {packDir}, the pack's folder. Its environment has GLIMMERVOID_PR_URL, GLIMMERVOID_PR_REPO, GLIMMERVOID_PR_NUMBER and GLIMMERVOID_PR_HEAD. It must print the source output JSON (glimmervoid packs guide --schema pr-flows) on stdout; anything else shows as an error on the pull request

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds before the command is stopped

repos.description: The owner/name repositories this applies to; every repository when absent

actions.description: Commands rules run on one review item with run:<id>; they print {"outcome":"done|started|refused|failed","message":"..."} and are limited to repositories only through the rules that name them

id.description: Unique within its list; inside a pack it is shown as <pack>/<id>

label.description: The name shown to the operator; rules never match on it

command.description: The program and its arguments, run without a shell from the Glimmervoid home folder; an argument may hold {prUrl}, {repo}, {number}, {head}, {itemPath}, {itemLine}, and in a pack also {packDir}, the pack's folder. Its environment has GLIMMERVOID_PR_URL, GLIMMERVOID_PR_REPO, GLIMMERVOID_PR_NUMBER and GLIMMERVOID_PR_HEAD, and the review item as GLIMMERVOID_ITEM_JSON. Exit 0 means done and any other exit failed, unless stdout prints the action outcome JSON (glimmervoid packs guide --schema pr-flows)

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds before the command is stopped

rules.description: Run after your own config.json rules; the first rule that matches an item decides it

name.description: Shown in the Handled list beside each item the rule decided

sources.description: The bare ids of this pack's sources the rule acts on. An item merged from several sources matches only when every one of them is listed here or under authors; any source when both are absent

authors.description: The GitHub logins of review comment authors this rule acts on, compared case-insensitively. An item merged from several sources matches only when every one of them is listed here or under authors; any source when both are absent

priority.description: The finding priorities this rule acts on; any priority when absent

paths.description: Repository paths; an entry ending in / matches every path under it, any other matches that exact path

text.description: Text the finding must contain, compared case-insensitively

scope.description: Rules act only on your own pull requests today, so mine and both act there and team never acts yet

repos.description: The owner/name repositories this applies to; every repository when absent

action.description: ask waits for you, fix-local hands the item to a local session, dismiss replies with reason and resolves it, run:<id> runs that action; run:<id> names an action of this pack by its bare id

reason.description: The reply posted when the rule dismisses an item

ui.description: Themes and panels this pack adds to the dashboard

themes.description: Color themes added to the Theme picker

label.description: The name shown in the Theme picker

mode.description: Whether the theme is dark or light, which picks the terminal palette its ANSI colors are tuned for

accentAnsiSlot.description: The terminal ANSI color the accent replaces, with a lighter mix of it as that color's bright variant; none leaves terminal colors alone

bg-card.description: Cards, panes and the terminal background

bg-surface.description: Raised controls: chips, inputs, menus and hover fills

border-dim.description: Faint dividers inside a card or list

border-hover.description: Borders of a hovered or focused control

text-dim.description: Secondary text such as hints and empty states

text-muted.description: Labels and metadata, between text and text-dim

accent.description: Links, focus rings, selection and primary actions

accent-dim.description: A quieter accent for selected borders

chrome.description: Dashboard colors; each key becomes the CSS custom property --<key>

running.description: The color of a running session, as --state-running

waiting.description: The color of a waiting session, as --state-waiting

failed.description: The color of a failed session, as --state-failed

monitoring.description: The color of a monitoring session, as --state-monitoring

done.description: The color of a done session, as --state-done

initializing.description: The color of a initializing session, as --state-initializing

idle.description: The color of a idle session, as --state-idle

starting.description: The color of a starting session, as --state-starting

complete.description: The color of a complete session, as --state-complete

states.description: One color per session state, shown as --state-<state> on cards, dots and badges

id.description: Unique within its list in this pack, and scoped to the pack name so it never clashes with another pack

panels.description: HTML pages shown as dashboard tabs, each sandboxed with no network and talking to the dashboard only through the panel bridge

id.description: Unique within its list in this pack, and scoped to the pack name so it never clashes with another pack

label.description: The tab name of the panel in the dashboard

entry.description: The HTML page the panel opens, relative to the pack folder

icon.description: An .svg file in the pack shown beside the panel label

reads.description: The bridge topics this panel may receive; the operator sees them before approving, and a subscribe for any other topic is ignored

acts.description: What this panel may do as the operator, without asking again: reviews lets it post, discard or requeue team reviews and resolve their threads, open an agent session on a pull request, merge your pull requests, turn merge when ready on or off, turn keep mergeable on or off, dismiss review items, hand them to a session or run their actions, reopen handled review items, save rules to your config, approve PR flow commands, run PR actions; sessions lets it start an agent session with any prompt in any project, and type text into any live session on this machine, using the pack sessions settings; the operator sees it before approving

launchers.description: Buttons in the Add session picker, each starting a session with its own prompt

id.description: Unique within its list in this pack, and scoped to the pack name so it never clashes with another pack

label.description: The button text, also the name of the session it starts

project.description: owner/name: the first configured project whose origin is that GitHub repository; or an absolute path of a folder on this machine. A launcher whose project matches nothing shows disabled

model.description: The model passed to the agent, as its own --model flag takes it; absent uses the agent default

effort.description: The reasoning effort passed to the agent, such as low, medium or high; absent uses the agent default

prompt.description: The first prompt the session gets

schedule.description: A cron pattern of five fields in the operator timezone; the launcher also starts its session on this schedule, skipping a run while its last scheduled session is still live, and catching up runs missed while Glimmervoid was down only with catchUp

catchUp.description: With a schedule, start one run at once when a scheduled run fell while Glimmervoid was down or the host slept; off skips missed runs

sessions.description: Permission settings for every session this pack starts

dangerouslySkipPermissions.description: Sessions this pack starts skip the agent's permission prompts; the operator sees it before approving

saneYolo.description: With dangerouslySkipPermissions, also catch risky commands with Sane YOLO; absent follows the operator's default

status.description: Status pages its panels read through the providers topic

urls.description: Statuspage summary URLs, such as https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/summary.json; the providers topic carries their open incidents

agent.description: Context and skills every session's agent gets once the operator approves the pack

context.description: A file in the pack that every session's first prompt names, so the agent reads it when the task touches what it covers; the operator reads it word for word before approving

skills.description: Skill folders in the pack, each holding a SKILL.md; every session gets them, as /<pack>:<folder name> on Claude Code and <pack>-<folder name> on Codex and Kimi Code

mcp.description: MCP servers every session gets once the pack is approved. Glimmervoid releases after 0.62.8 read it; older ones refuse a manifest that sets it

name.description: The name every agent lists the server under; a server the operator registered under the same name gives way to this one in glimmervoid sessions

url.description: The streamable HTTP MCP endpoint; with no secret the agent signs in through its own MCP OAuth login

secret.description: A bearer token sent to this server: glimmervoid reads the name from the vault at session start once the operator allows it for the project, and passes it by environment variable, never argv; while it is denied or cannot be read, a Gemini CLI or Kimi Code session fails its sign-in and any other session leaves the server out

servers.description: MCP servers every locally launched glimmervoid session gets once the operator approves the pack
